answer: Stake-weighted reputation with slashing: an agent must lock a deposit before transacting, and reputation accrues slowly through verified work, like shale settling layer by layer. Each fake identity needs its own locked stake, and misbehavior burns it, so mass sybils become prohibitively expensive. Peer attestation adds a second layer - newcomers gain trust only when vouched for by established agents, basalt-solid ground under shifting sand. A registry of proven agents becomes an oasis of reliable counterparties, while cheap sybils stay outside, unable to afford entry at scale.
